findings: Backend imports deleted categoryService — adminRoutes.js and publicRoutes.js import categoryService from ../services/categoryService.js. If that file was deleted (frontend pages were), the server will crash on startup or when the route module loads. Remove category imports and routes from both files.

Add-on backend routes and service still present — addonService.js exists, adminRoutes.js and publicRoutes.js expose /addons endpoints, and publicRoutes.js serves GET /addons to the frontend. CartPage still calls publicApi.getAddOns() and displays add-ons in a decorative section. The add-ons feature was only removed from admin management UI, not from the system. Either remove add-on service and routes entirely, or document that add-ons are view-only for customers.

Product schema mismatch between frontend and backend — productService.js validates and stores categoryId, addOnIds, shortDescription, servingSize, ingredients, allergens, storageInstructions, nutritionalInfo, labels, and additionalImages. ProductFormModal only submits name, description, basePrice, imageUrl, isAvailable, and slug. Backend will either reject the product or store it with undefined values for expected fields. Simplify productService.js sanitizeProduct to match the five-field frontend schema.

Custom add-ons field not wired to backend — CheckoutPage relabeled the notes textarea to Special Instructions or Add-ons but still stores it in formData.notes. The backend orderService.js stores notes as a generic text field. This works but is cosmetic only — the label change doesn't actually create a structured add-ons field, and the backend doesn't distinguish special instructions from add-on requests. Clarify whether this is intentional (free-form text) or if structured add-ons are needed.

CartPage still fetches and displays add-ons — CartPage.jsx calls publicApi.getAddOns(), stores them in state, and renders an Enhance Your Order with Add-ons section below cart items. This contradicts the requirement to remove add-ons from the system. Remove the loadAddOns() call, addOns state, and the add-ons promotional section.
